item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Mon Oct 5, 7:00 PM — NJ
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: Montclair Music Club - Season Opening Concert - Oct. 5 — Mon Oct 5, 7:30 PM — The Presbyterian Church of Upper Montclair
item.description: Announcing the Montclair Music Club 2026-‘27 Season Opening Concert, Monday evening, October 5th, 7:30 pm, Presbyterian Church of Upper Montclair, 53 Norwood Avenue. You are invited to share in this season’s opener featuring the newly former Kintsugi Quintet performing the Prokofiev Quintet in G minor; coloratura soprano Karen Lundry with pianist Barry Spatz and actor Joseph Smith performing arias by Gounod and Bellini; lutist and guitarist Daryl Hester playing pieces by Ballard, Galileia and Towner; and tenor Kristopher Jean, with pianist Ryan Bridge, singing works by Donizetti, Lehar, Ricky Ian Gordon and closing with Flaherty’s Make Them Hear You from Ragtime. Reception immediately following the program. Donations welcome. Please share this announcement with family and friends. Enter the church on the east side of the building at the double doors. item.title: Holding Space for Queer Social Change Through Pop Culture — Wed Oct 7, 5:30 PM — SBUS 140
item.description: What does it take to create lasting social change - and what can the history of LGBTQ+ activism teach us about today's battles over education, identity, and civil rights? Join journalist and cultural commentator Tracy E. Gilchrist, host of Holding Space with Tracy E. Gilchrist and former editor-in-chief of The Advocate for a lively conversation with Professor Lisa M. Stulberg, NYU sociologist of education and author of the new book How to Win a Culture War: LGBTQ+ Social Change Through Pop Culture. Drawing on Stulberg's research into LGBTQ+ social movements, education, and political change-and Gilchrist's years covering the intersections of LGBTQ+ equality, politics, and popular culture-the conversation will explore how movements change public attitudes, institutions, and policy; why cultural conflicts become so powerful; and what history can teach us about navigating the culture wars of the present. item.title: Mount Vernon Trail Hike — Sun Oct 11, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for this point to point hike, the next in our 911 National Memorial Trail series, this with the Mt Vernon Trail being the subject. The official trail map shows this as a part of it, as a spur. The trail is just over 17 miles, so it fits perfectly what we do, and after this one we'll start heading back toward NYC. After meeting at the end point, we'll shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to our start point. The Mt Vernon Trail is pretty straightforward, and follows the Potomac River the entire time, so it's really a great continuation from what we've already done with the C&O. This time I'm only planning on one day of hiking, and might visit some museums the second day. If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374
Source: Meetup: Metrotrails Hiking

item.title: Susquehanna Super Hike — Sun Oct 25, 9:00 AM
item.description: Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! It's been a long time since we've done a more difficult hike like this, but it's been a long time coming. Since the son is going to "Trunk or Treat" with his mom, it is an opportunity to complete the final difficult section of the Conestoga Trail, as well as the next bit of the Mason-Dixon Trail in our rebooted series that we'd put on hold. This promises to be challenging, but also very rewarding with views, history, and more. After meeting at Pequea boat launch, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to our start point north of the Norman Wood Bridge. We'll follow the Mason-Dixon Trail up to an overlook, and then down through a scenic gorge with small waterfalls. We then get on the towpath of the old Susquehanna and Tidewater Canal to Lock 12.
